title: Finding the Turn That Mattered in a Long Agent Rollout
hook: RL with verifiable rewards scores a whole trajectory pass/fail, which tells an agent nothing about which of its forty turns was the pivotal one. AgentOPSD recovers turn-level credit without a critic.
key_points: Outcome-only rewards give one number per trajectory, so the few decisions that actually determined success get no distinct signal.
AgentOPSD aggregates token-level teacher–student log-probability gaps into turn-level evidence.
It then updates a Bayesian belief state in log-odds space, recursively, across the turns of the rollout.
Pivotal turns are identified by the marginal belief revision between consecutive states.
Critic-free: it drops into standard policy optimization with no extra value network and no extra rollouts.
On ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA it beat GRPO and self-distillation baselines, hitting 89.1% success on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-7B.
content_html: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become the standard recipe for training agents, but it hands back a single number for an entire trajectory. In a forty-turn task, that number is spread evenly over turns that were decisive and turns that were bookkeeping. Recent work has tried privileged self-distillation to get denser supervision; what stayed unclear is how those local signals should compose into sequential credit.
extra_html:
The construction

AgentOPSD, from Wang and colleagues, works in two steps. First it aggregates token-level log-probability gaps between a teacher and the student policy into a single piece of evidence per turn. Then it treats the rollout as a filtering problem: a Bayesian belief state, maintained in log-odds space, is updated recursively turn by turn. The reweighting that falls out converts sparse outcome supervision into per-turn credit, and the turns where the belief revises most sharply are read as the pivotal ones.

The practical appeal is what it doesn't need — no critic network, no additional rollouts, and compatibility with standard policy optimization. On ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA with Qwen2.5 at 3B and 7B, it outperformed GRPO and strong self-distillation baselines, reaching 89.1% success on ALFWorld at 7B. Ablations attribute the gains specifically to the turn-level aggregation and the history-dependent recursive update, rather than to denser supervision alone.

related.title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
related.hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

related.title: TRACE: Turn-Level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
related.hook: A failed agent rollout might still contain dozens of genuinely useful actions — outcome-only RL punishes every one of them the same as the final mistake. TRACE assigns credit per tool call instead, with no extra critic.

related.hook: NVIDIA's bet: an agentic RL codebase small enough for a researcher — or a coding assistant — to hold in their head entirely, without giving up performance.

flashcards.prompt: What is the credit-assignment problem in agentic RL with verifiable rewards?
flashcards.back_html: The reward arrives once, at the end of a long multi-turn trajectory. Advantage estimates are therefore trajectory-level, so the handful of pivotal decisions that actually determined the outcome receive no signal distinguishing them from the routine ones.

flashcards.prompt: Where does AgentOPSD get its per-turn learning signal from?

choices.text: Token-level teacher–student log-probability gaps, aggregated up to the turn level
A learned critic network that predicts the value of each intermediate state
Extra rollouts branched from every turn to estimate its counterfactual value

flashcards.explanation_html: AgentOPSD is deliberately critic-free and needs no extra rollouts: it turns log-probability gaps between teacher and student into turn-level evidence, then folds that evidence into a recursive Bayesian belief update.

flashcards.prompt: How does AgentOPSD decide which turns were pivotal?
flashcards.back_html: By the size of the marginal belief revision between consecutive states — a turn that sharply moves the log-odds belief state is one that mattered.
